firepit_lever_findings.root_cause_read: Two independent prompt strategies (a soft pin in iter1, an explicit authorized override in iter2) both failed to remove the ring across 4 total Gemini-styled candidates (1 in iter1 on the selected anchor + 3 in iter2 on all iter1 anchors), plus 3 raw anchors inspected pre-Gemini in iter1's best-of-3 rejection step. This is now a well-tested negative result: the artifact is not prompt-controllable at the Gemini re-registration stage within this recipe -- it most likely reflects a strong learned prior in the model's own depiction of campfire-lit ground (reinforced by the anchor image already showing the pattern), not something addressable by instruction wording alone at this stage. Fixing it would need a stage the task did not authorize testing (e.g. inpainting the ring region as an isolated post-process, or retraining/prompting the base LoRA mint itself away from radial falloff, or swapping the base recipe's control image away from a bare point-light depth cue) -- out of scope for this 2-iteration pass.

verdict: NOT CONVERGED. Candidate (A) median 6.0 vs incumbent (B) median 7.0 vs disguised real-art control (C) median 9.0 (in-band, valid) -- identical to iter1's read. Ceiling for this pass is median 6.0, below the >=7.0 target and roughly flat vs the original outdoor-lora smoke test's 6.5. Across 2 iterations, 3 raw anchor candidates (best-of-3, iter1), and 4 total Gemini-styled candidates (1 in iter1 + 3 in iter2), neither firepit-pin phrasing (soft request in iter1, explicit structure-lock-exception override in iter2) nor the lorasScale 0.6-0.7 sweep measurably reduced the concentric-ring artifact; best-of-N rejection found no clean winner in either iteration because all candidates were similarly affected. Recommend NOT adopting either candidate; the firepit artifact is a confirmed, reproducible ceiling on this LoRA+recipe combination for camp, not a tuning gap this pass's levers can close.
